\section[\hi{शुभ} \hi{रात्रि}]{\hi{शुभ} \hi{रात्रि} (śubh rātri) — "good night," the formal doublet in action}

\label{lesson:HI-C27-shubh-raatri}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Warm-up.} {[}PAUSE 2s{]} Hindi keeps two versions of "night" side by side — one for everyday speech, one for set phrases. Here's where the formal one gets used.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know — \hi{शुभ} \hi{रात्रि} — "auspicious night"}
\textbf{\hi{शुभ} \hi{रात्रि}} (\textbf{śubh rātri}) — "\textbf{good night}" — literally "\textbf{auspicious night}." Notice: this uses \textbf{\hi{रात्रि}} (\emph{rātri}), the very Sanskrit word last lesson's \emph{raat} descended \textbf{from} — but here, kept in its \textbf{full, unworn Sanskrit} form. This is a classic \textbf{tatsama/tadbhava doublet}: \emph{rātri} (\textbf{tatsama}, a direct, unchanged Sanskrit borrowing) sits alongside \emph{raat} (\textbf{tadbhava}, the same word worn down by centuries of ordinary sound change) — Hindi keeps both, one for everyday speech, one for set formal phrases like this one.

\subsection*{You'll want to know — \hi{शुभ} — "auspicious," from a root meaning "to shine"}
\textbf{\hi{शुभ}} (\textbf{śubh}) — "\textbf{auspicious, good, fortunate}" — comes from the Sanskrit verbal root \textbf{\hi{शुभ्}} (\emph{śubh}), whose core sense is "\textbf{to be beautiful, splendid}." This traces to a well-sourced \textbf{Proto-Indo-European} root, \emph{\textbf{*\'{k}ewb\textsuperscript{h}-}} ("to be beautiful"). Some scholars propose a \textbf{further, more speculative} connection beyond that — to \emph{*(s)kewh\textsubscript{1}-} ("to perceive") or \emph{*\'{k}ew-} ("to shine") — but that deeper link, not the \emph{*\'{k}ewb\textsuperscript{h}-} root itself, is the genuinely uncertain part. Either way, the underlying idea is a familiar one: \textbf{auspiciousness imagined as a kind of radiance or beauty} — something good "shines."

\subsection*{Guided Practice}
{[}PAUSE 1s{]}

\begin{itemize}

  \item {[}YOU SAY: "śubh rātri" — "good night," literally "auspicious night"{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: the formal doublet — rātri here, raat in everyday speech{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: śubh's own root — śubh, "to shine" $\to$ "auspicious"{]}
\end{itemize}
